_why: SEC-105. Dated, owned exceptions to the npm-audit gate.
An advisory with no patched version is not a bug you can fix — it is a
decision you have to take. Before this file existed there was nowhere to
record that decision, so the only options were an emergency override pin or
a frozen pipeline. SEC-88 took the second: eleven days, 40+ green PRs held,
twelve tested security fixes kept out of production. SEC-94 took the first,
and the resulting blanket brace-expansion pin crashed `npm run lint`.
Hygiene is enforced by scripts/check-waiver-hygiene.py (CTL-025): every
entry needs advisory + package + severity + ticket + owner + reason, and
exactly one of `expires` (a real risk accepted temporarily — FAILS the
build on lapse) or `review_by` (accepted by design — notifies on lapse).
`expires` may be at most 12 months out.
Note the direction of the expiry failure, which is deliberate and is the
opposite of what several commercial tools do: Snyk's own docs concede that
a malformed `expires` means the ignore 'will be respected and persist
indefinitely'. Theirs fails OPEN. This one fails CLOSED — a lapsed or
unparseable date reddens the build rather than silently granting forever.
EMPTY IS THE CORRECT STEADY STATE. An entry here is a known-unfixable
finding being carried on purpose, not a way to quiet a noisy gate. Fix the
advisory if it has a fix.
